claims.text: Adding 2–5 wt% Si to ZrB2 and spark-plasma sintering at 1500–1700 °C will produce a continuous amorphous silica-rich grain-boundary phase.
The silica-rich grain-boundary phase will enhance densification at 1500–1700 °C.
The proposed Si addition will improve the mechanical strength of the resulting ZrB2 composite.
The silica-rich phase will form a self-healing protective scale during high-temperature exposure.
The protective scale will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The silica-rich grain-boundary phase or scale will improve resistance to corrosion by liquid plating metals.
Silicon will react during SPS to form silica along ZrB2 grain boundaries under vacuum or inert processing conditions.
The grain-boundary silica layer will enhance mass transport during sintering.
Enhanced mass transport will permit ZrB2 densification at a lower temperature than conventional processing.
The silica layer will act as a barrier during liquid-metal exposure.
Strict control of Si content, atmosphere, and temperature can suppress unwanted silicide formation.
The proposed process will yield a densified, low-porosity ZrB2 composite.
The proposed composite will have greater mechanical strength than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
The proposed composite will have better oxidation durability than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
The proposed composite will have better liquid-metal corrosion resistance than high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing above 2300 °C.
Low-temperature ZrB2 specimens without Si doping have inadequate oxidation resistance.
Low-temperature ZrB2 specimens without Si doping have inadequate liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
The predicted benefits apply within a processing window of 1500–1700 °C under vacuum or inert atmosphere.
